claims.text: Adding Cr to refractory high-entropy alloys can improve their high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Cr addition promotes formation of a protective oxide layer on the alloy surface.
The protective oxide layer reduces oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Reduced oxygen diffusion improves high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Cr-modified refractory high-entropy alloys will have better high-temperature oxygen resistance than otherwise untreated refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed improvement applies under high-temperature conditions.
The exact mechanism of improved oxygen resistance is not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The mechanism field presents a definite protective-oxide and oxygen-diffusion pathway, while the uncertainty field states that the exact mechanism is not fully understood. This is a tension in confidence rather than a direct contradiction of the proposed pathway.
